sections.h2: Where does an Alpharetta seller start?
sections.html:
Alpharetta owners generally choose among a full agent listing, a private sale, and a cash purchase that closes when the seller says. With a typical home value of $649,000 in Census figures, even small differences in condition and timing can move the final number a long way.

The city sits in northern Fulton County, about 26 miles north of downtown Atlanta. It went by Milton until July 1858, was chartered as Alpharetta on December 11, 1858, and served as the seat of Milton County until 1931, when that county folded into Fulton to avoid bankruptcy during the Great Depression.

Alpharetta covers 26.9 square miles of land and touches Johns Creek, Roswell, Milton and unincorporated Forsyth County. The climate is humid subtropical and falls in USDA hardiness zone 7b, which shapes what landscaping lasts and how mature trees shade a lot.

  • A listing makes sense for a move-in ready house that can be staged and shown to several bidders.
  • A private sale suits an owner who can price from nearby closed sales and has an attorney ready.
  • A cash sale helps with a probate property, a house needing big updates, or a relocation with little lead time.

sections.h2: What do Alpharetta's Census figures reveal about its housing?
sections.html:
This is an owner-occupied, high-income city. The July 2025 estimate is 66,921 residents, up 1.7 percent from the 65,810 base used for April 2020.

Roughly 27.8 percent of residents were born abroad and 32.8 percent speak a language other than English at home, a mix that reflects the global employers based in town.

sections.h2: Which companies and amenities bring buyers to Alpharetta?
sections.html:
Corporate offices lead the list. City economic development figures from February 2026 show Fiserv with 2,087 employees, ADP with 2,074, MCI (Verizon) with 1,928 and Equifax with 1,722, followed by Jackson Healthcare, Morgan Stanley, UPS Supply Chain Solutions, Toyota Motor Credit and Ernst and Young.

Downtown Alpharetta, the 86-acre Avalon district that opened in 2014, and the City Center complex add walkable dining and shopping, while North Point Mall is set for redevelopment. The Big Creek Greenway and the Alpha Loop, a trail system that now runs more than six miles, give neighborhoods near the paths a recreation draw.

No MARTA trains stop in Alpharetta, though bus routes link it to the rest of metro Atlanta.

Fulton County Schools serves the city, and Alpharetta High School serves most of it. Families sometimes also look at Cambridge, Centennial, Chattahoochee, Johns Creek, Milton, Northview and Roswell high schools, depending on the address.

Elementary schools listed for the city include Abbotts Hill, Alpharetta Elementary, Creek View, Dolvin, Lake Windward, Manning Oaks and New Prospect, and Amana Academy is a public charter for kindergarten through eighth grade. Perimeter College at Georgia State University, Gwinnett Technical College and Reinhardt University each have a campus here. Confirm the attendance zone with the school district before putting a school name in your listing.

sections.h2: Is the address inside Alpharetta city limits?
sections.html:
An Alpharetta mailing address does not guarantee the property lies inside the city. The Halcyon mixed-use district has an Alpharetta postal address yet sits in Forsyth County, outside both the city limits and Fulton County.

That changes who bills the property. The City of Alpharetta levies its own ad valorem tax for city operations and voter-approved bonds and keeps its own homestead exemption page, while Fulton County sets the assessment. A parcel in a neighboring jurisdiction owes tax to different governments. Check your tax bill, or ask the Fulton County Board of Assessors which governments tax your parcel before you quote carrying costs to a buyer.

sections.h2: How do Fulton County assessment appeals work for Alpharetta owners?
sections.html:
Every Fulton property receives a yearly notice of assessment, and an owner who doubts the stated fair market value may appeal within 45 days of the notice date. Only the value can be appealed, not the estimated tax, and the right lapses after the date printed on the notice.

  • File online, by mail, or in person at one of five county locations, including the North Fulton center at 7741 Roswell Road NE, Suite 210.
  • Choose a Board of Equalization hearing, non-binding arbitration on value, or a Hearing Officer; the last two may carry fees.
  • Expect months of review, and pay any temporary bill sent meanwhile to avoid penalties.

If an appeal is still open when you sell, tell your closing attorney so the settlement figures account for it.

sections.h2: Which city services and permits matter when selling in Alpharetta?
sections.html:
The city's Apply menu gathers the forms a seller may need: a permitting portal, building construction permits, business licenses, homestead exemptions, and a form to establish or end trash service. Water and sewer bills are paid to Fulton County, so closing that account is a separate step from ending city trash service.

The city also keeps a Short-Term Rentals page under its Business section. If you plan to tell a buyer the house can host nightly guests, get the current rules from the city's planning and zoning staff in writing first. Work such as a deck, a finished basement or a new HVAC system should be checked against the permitting portal so no open permit holds up the closing.

sections.h2: How does the deed transfer tax apply to an Alpharetta sale?
sections.html:
Georgia treats the real estate transfer tax as an excise tax on the sale and not as a property tax, and it must be paid before the deed is recorded. For Alpharetta, the recording office is the Fulton County Clerk of Superior Court, and the state recording authority supplies the electronic PT-61 form that reports the sale.

The seller owes the tax unless the contract says otherwise. The Department of Revenue sends questions on taxability and exemptions to the county clerk, so raise any gift, family or trust transfer with that office before closing.

faqs.q: How far apart are Alpharetta's home values and Albany's?
faqs.a: Very far. The Census Bureau lists $649,000 for Alpharetta's typical owner-occupied home against $124,300 in Albany and $299,200 in Athens-Clarke County for 2020-2024.

faqs.q: What is the cutoff for a Fulton appeal on Alpharetta property?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the date on the Notice of Assessment. The date printed on your notice controls, and the appeal covers value only.

faqs.q: Does a 30004 or 30005 mailing address prove the house is in the city?
faqs.a: No. Halcyon, for instance, uses an Alpharetta address but sits in Forsyth County. Check your tax bill or ask the Fulton County Board of Assessors.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer tax in an Alpharetta contract?
faqs.a: The seller is liable under Georgia's rule, and the contract may assign the cost to the buyer. Ask your closing attorney to confirm the amount before the settlement date.

faqs.q: What should I do about an unfinished permit before selling?
faqs.a: Ask the city's building permit staff through the permitting portal what is open on the address, and tell the buyer about any permit that has not been finished and approved.
